probe: Audit official IPFS Bitswap and Kademlia DHT specifications to determine whether a CID-addressed raw block can be returned as block bytes and whether provider discovery supplies any passive independently pre-existing availability primitive that avoids required publication/pinning/hosted storage.

observations: Bitswap is specified as sending and receiving content-addressed blocks.
Bitswap 1.1 payload entries contain a CID prefix and a data byte field; the protocol therefore transports block data bytes associated with the requested CID.
The spec does not itself guarantee that an arbitrary requested block already has an available provider.
Provider records associate a CID/multihash with peers providing the content; the DHT stores provider records rather than the content itself.
A provider advertises by sending ADD_PROVIDER records to DHT servers.
Provider records have 48h validity and providers SHOULD republish every 22h; lookup can fail when no provider records are found.

reasoning: For the narrow transport question, the official Bitswap wire format supports returning block data bytes for a requested CID, so no mandatory payload transformation is evident at this layer.

For the availability question, the official routing specification explicitly separates provider records from content and requires providers to advertise and periodically republish records; lookups may return no provider.

Therefore the IPFS protocol specifications do not establish passive independently pre-existing availability of an arbitrary raw Git-preimage block. End-to-end retrieval still depends on some peer already storing and serving the block or on an additional publication/storage mechanism.

Because the Phase-1 route requires zero residual richer-mode/protected/manual execution, zero finite monthly/trial/paid quota dependency and zero incremental cost, this candidate cannot pass on protocol semantics alone.
tested_scope: Official Bitswap protocol specification and current IPFS Kademlia DHT provider-record specification only, plus own r329 continuation. No live publication, pinning, gateway fetch, DHT query, provider lookup, Bitswap transfer, hosted storage, swarm residency, external mutation, or protected execution was performed.
scope_negative: No claim that public gateways, DHT/IPNI, pinning services, or arbitrary peers provide permanent or quota-free residency; no claim of exact end-to-end retrieval for the candidate; no claim about git-raw codec or SHA-256 alternatives.

frontier: Bitswap can transport block data bytes bound to a CID, addressing the narrow retrieval-byte-format question at the protocol layer.
DHT provider records do not store content and require provider advertisement/republishing; they do not establish passive arbitrary-block residency.
The cidv1 raw+sha1 mirror remains fail-closed because a zero-quota, zero-cost, no-manual-action availability primitive is still missing.

A higher-value next direction is to test a repository-native immutable-object reconstruction mechanism that may eliminate external content residency entirely rather than trying to prove free passive IPFS storage.
